summary: This benchmark investigates whether a 14.3M-parameter transformer requires exact register memory addresses or merely consistent, predictable addressing to solve an associative-recall register task. Through carefully controlled ablations (stable cyclic shift, matched-density random routing, dense baseline, and post-training routing interventions), the authors demonstrate that the model preserves high balanced accuracy (92.26% vs. 93.30%) under a systematic one-event displacement, while random addressing drops accuracy to chance levels (9.06%). The study features sound experimental controls and bootstrap confidence intervals, but is limited by testing on a single seed and synthetic task without an uploaded reproducible code artifact.
strengths: Clean isolation of variables: the random routing control exactly matches the eligible query-dependent write density, ruling out token-count cues as the driver of performance.
Strong statistical reporting, including paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for both validation and test sets.
Well-designed inference-time ablation controls demonstrating that models cannot adapt dynamically to displaced or randomized routing without joint training.
Transparent documentation of model hyperparameters, optimizer steps, runtime environment, and explicit limitations regarding seed variance.
weaknesses: All reported training runs rely on a single initialization seed (seed 101), leaving training-seed variance unquantified.
No supporting repository was directly provided with the submission, restricting verification to the text and external links (resulting in a text_only badge).

The evaluation is restricted to a narrow, synthetic 256-token register-update task, meaning the findings do not directly transfer to real-world code or natural language reasoning without further evaluation.
suggestions: Run evaluations across at least 3 to 5 random initialization seeds to report seed-level confidence intervals alongside program-paired bootstrap intervals.
Attach the source code repository directly to the submission artifact to allow automated reproducibility auditing and qualify for verified badges.
Test displacement variations beyond a single-event shift (e.g., multi-step shifts or non-cyclic offsets) to determine the limits of positional translation invariance.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Zoology: Measuring and Improving Recall in Efficient Language Models
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While Zoology benchmarks multi-query associative recall across attention and sub-quadratic architectures, this submission specifically analyzes the internal routing tolerance of attention by comparing ground-truth, shifted, and randomized register addresses.
